senses.definition: (intransitive, Northern England, Scotland) To go; walk; proceed.

quotes.text: (Colin alone) Ah, Colin, thou’rt a prodigal; a thriftless loon thou’st been, that cou’d na’ keep a little pelf to thysall when thou had’st got it; now thou may’st gang in this poor geer to thy live's end, and worse too for aught I can tell; ’faith, mon, ’twas a smeart little bysack of money thou hadst scrap’d together, an the best part of it had na’ being last amongst thy kinsfolk, in the Isles of Skey and Mull; muckle gude may it do the weams of them that ha’ it! There was Jamie MacGregor and Sawney MacNab, and the twa braw lads of Kinruddin, with old Charley MacDougall, my mother's first husband's second cousin: by my sol I cou’d na’ see such near relations, and gentlemen of sich auncient families gang upon bare feet, while I rode a horseback: I had been na’ true Scot, an I cou’d na’ ge’en a countryman a gude last upon occasion (as he is going out, Miss Aubrey enters.)
quotes.reference: 1772, Richard Cumberland, The Fashionable Lover. A Comedy., act III:

quotes.text: "And am I to meet my Mary at Moffat? Come away, little, dear, welcome body, thou blessed of heaven, come away, and taste of an auld shepherd's best cheer, and I'll gang foot for foot with you to Moffat, and my auld wife shall gang foot for foot with us too. I tell you, little, blessed, and welcome crile, come along with me."

senses.definition: A number going in company; a number of friends or persons associated for a particular purpose.
examples: The gang from our office is going out for drinks Friday night.

senses.definition: A group of laborers under one foreman; a squad or workgang.
examples: a gang of sailors; a railroad gang; a labor gang or pool.

senses.definition: A criminal group with a common cultural background and identifying features, often associated with a particular section of a city.
examples: a youth gang; a neighborhood gang; motorcycle gang.

senses.definition: A group of criminals or alleged criminals who band together for mutual protection and profit.
examples: The Winter Hill Gang was quite proficient at murdering rival mobsters in order to take over their rackets.

senses.definition: A group of politicians united in furtherance of a political goal.
examples: The Gang of Four was led by Jiang Qing, the fourth wife of Mao Zedong.
Not all members of the Gang of Six are consistent in their opposition to filibuster.

senses.definition: A combination of similar tools or implements arranged so as, by acting together, to save time or labor; a set.
examples: a gang of saws; a gang of plows; a gang drill; gang milling.

senses.definition: A set; all required for an outfit.
(electrics) A number of switches or other electrical devices wired into one unit and covered by one faceplate.
examples: an outlet gang box; a double gang switch.

senses.definition: (electrics) A group of wires attached as a bundle.
examples: Do a drop for the telephone gang, then another drop for the Internet gang, both through the ceiling of the wiring closet.

senses.definition: (now chiefly dialectal) A going, journey; a course, path, track.

quotes.text: In unploughed Maine he sought the lumberers’ gang / Where from a hundred lakes young rivers sprang
That week was also called the Gang Week, from the Saxon ganger, to go; and the Rogation days were termed the Gang Days.

(African-American Vernacular, used in the vocative) A term of address for a group, particularly when cautioning them or offering advice.

subsenses.definition: (by extension, Internet slang) A term of address for any other person or group of people.
examples: The sun isn't real? What are you even talking about, gang?

senses.definition: (transitive) To attach similar items together to form a larger unit.

quotes.text: Volume controls may be ganged to mode switches to provide maximum output […]
